judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'All records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business' and 'all confidential information or trade secrets ... including, but not limited to' client names — an open-ended catch-all whose outer edge (publicly available client identities) is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works together with 11(b) and 12(a) and is expressly backed by the injunction carve-out in 14(c); no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The surrender obligation is expressed in terms of 'Confidential Records or Documents', a phrase that never appears as a defined term — the defined term in 11(a) is 'Confidential Information and Documents' — so the scope of what must be returned is a drafting error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks 11(a) closely and is enforceable in court under 14(c) notwithstanding the arbitration clause, so the fit is mostly coherent apart from the mismatched label.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any Wells Fargo Advisors client that you had contact with or otherwise learned of' is extremely broad and 'solicit or cause or permit to be solicited' is undefined, making the boundary between announcement and solicitation the classic fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is reinforced by the confidentiality provisions and the 14(c) injunction carve-out, but sits in some tension with paragraph 7's at-will framing and with 10(b)(ii)(A)'s separate competition-based test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final clause, 'or discontinuing his or her employment with Wells Fargo Advisors', is grammatically detached from the verbs 'recruit, entice, induce or solicit', and 'any other lines of business in which Wells Fargo Advisors ... is engaged' is a catch-all after a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs parallel to 12(a) and is covered by 14(c) and paragraph 15's survival language, with no contradicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'you will be expected to contribute' is hortatory rather than obligatory, and the amount is 'determined after a consultation' with management 'pursuant to applicable legal considerations' — no ascertainable standard or cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 15 refers to surviving 'indemnification obligations' although this is the only clause resembling one, and 13(c) then treats these contributions as compensation adjustments; the fit is loose but not squarely contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'disciplinary action for trading errors that may have a financial impact on future earnings' is a garbled formulation, and 'accountable for' does not say what financial liability, if any, follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13(c) supplies the mechanism by charging errors against Net Eligible Revenue, so the two read together, though 'accountable' is never converted into a defined payment duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net Eligible Revenue' is capitalised as a defined term but is defined nowhere in this Agreement, and the parenthetical gloss 'i.e., charges spread beyond three (3) months' is an imperfect definition of an installment plan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on the New FA Compensation Plan, which paragraph 3 permits Wells Fargo Advisors to modify unilaterally, and it presupposes monthly compensation that paragraph 4 makes available only post-graduation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclosure bullets contain several textual defects ('Paragraph 1!4(b)', 'the arbitration forum in the claim is filed') and the exclusion list mixes State insurance claims with NLRA claims in a parenthetical whose scope is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tells the employee he is agreeing to arbitrate disputes with 'a client, or any other person', whereas the operative clause 14(b) reaches only controversies 'arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors' — a direct mismatch between the explanatory and operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is broad but its scope terms ('any controversy or dispute ... arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors') and its FINRA-then-AAA fallback are stated definitely; the reference to AAA 'Securities Arbitration Rules, effective May 1, 1993' names a rule set that no longer exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is narrower than the 14(a) disclosures (which promise arbitration of claims against clients and 'any other person') and is qualified by 14(c)'s court carve-out available only to the employer, so scope disputes turn on reading 14(a)-(c) together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is short and definite as to remedy and forum, but it is drafted entirely one-sidedly — only Wells Fargo Advisors may go to court — which is the kind of asymmetry construed against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out of 14(b)'s mandatory arbitration and out of the 14(a) representation that the employee gives up 'the right to sue ... in court', leaving open whether a court may decide the merits of paragraphs 11 and 12 or only grant interim relief.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lists surviving obligations 'including, but not limited to' three categories, one of which — 'indemnification obligations' — has no counterpart anywhere in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to indemnification obligations that the Agreement never creates, and the bar on the employee assigning against paragraph 1's 'its successors and assigns' language, make the survival scheme sit imperfectly with paragraphs 13 and 20.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence Missouri choice-of-law clause that expressly excludes renvoi; there is nothing in the wording to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is capable of friction with the Texas employment location and with the arbitration provisions' choice of forum rules, but no provision in the document contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence says invalidity 'shall not affect the validity or unenforceability of the remaining Provisions', which is a drafting slip that reverses the intended meaning, and the reformation instruction to a court is itself of doubtful operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the restrictive covenants in paragraphs 11 and 12 and the caption disclaimer harmonises with the headings used throughout; no conflict appears elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause preserves only the right to enforce 'any other breach of the same or any other covenant', which arguably concedes waiver as to the forgone breach itself, and it is drafted to protect only one party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the modification restriction in paragraph 8 and with the covenants in paragraphs 11 and 12; nothing elsewhere cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a pure acknowledgment of reading and understanding, with no operative obligation to construe, though its heading 'RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS' describes nothing in the paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 17 provides that captions do not affect meaning, which defuses the mislabelled heading; the acknowledgment otherwise fits paragraphs 11 and 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the entire understanding ... regarding the matters addressed herein' is a self-limiting integration clause whose scope depends on what counts as a matter addressed, and the survival sentence is circular ('provisions that require survival ... shall survive').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against paragraph 8's statement that the Agreement is 'only a synopsis' and paragraph 6's preservation of separate HR and compliance policies, and against paragraph 15's own list of surviving terms, leaving the integration and survival scheme internally uneven.
